titleEn: Humidity can make heatwaves more dangerous. It’s time to warn Australians about this threat
titleZh: 湿度会让热浪更危险，预警不应忽视这一点
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: It’s the build-up in northern Australia – the time of year when heat and humidity get worse ahead of the wet season. Common phrases such as “going troppo” or “mango madness” give a sense of the effects. Tempers fray and tensions rise.
paragraphs.zh: 这是澳大利亚北方的集结--一年中雨季到来之前，炎热和潮湿的天气会变得更糟。常见的短语，如"热带"或"芒果疯狂"，可以让人感觉到这种影响。脾气变坏，紧张局势加剧。

paragraphs.en: There’s now emerging evidence that humidity makes heat more dangerous. Humid heatwaves – where high temperatures combine with high humidity – are potentially more dangerous than dry heatwaves.
paragraphs.zh: 现在有新的证据表明，湿度使高温更危险。潮湿的热浪--高温联合收割机和高湿度结合在一起--比干燥的热浪更危险。

paragraphs.en: Elsewhere in the world, humid heatwaves are already claiming lives. Over 1,300 pilgrims died in Saudi Arabia in 2024 due to lethal levels of humidity and heat, while India and Pakistan have also been hard hit.
paragraphs.zh: 在世界其他地方，潮湿的热浪已经夺去了生命。2024年，沙特阿拉伯有1,300多名朝圣者死于致命的潮湿和高温，而印度和巴基斯坦也受到了严重打击。

paragraphs.en: Our recent research in the Northern Territory found more people came to emergency departments during intense humid heatwaves than comparable dry heatwaves.
paragraphs.zh: 我们最近在北领地的研究发现，在强烈的潮湿热浪中，来急诊室的人比可比的干燥热浪要多。

paragraphs.en: The problem is, we’re not warning people about this combined threat. Australia’s heatwave warning systems focus only on temperature – not on humidity.
paragraphs.zh: 问题是，我们并没有警告人们这种综合威胁。澳大利亚的热浪预警系统只关注温度，而不是湿度。

paragraphs.en: Why humidity matters
paragraphs.zh: 为什么湿度很重要

paragraphs.en: Intense heat stresses the body. Humidity can make this worse.
paragraphs.zh: 高温会给身体带来压力。潮湿会使情况变得更糟。

paragraphs.en: The human body relies heavily on sweating to regulate temperature. When sweat evaporates from the skin, it removes heat and helps keep the body cool. When humidity is high, evaporation doesn’t work as well and it’s harder for the body to release heat and stay cool.
paragraphs.zh: 人体很大程度上依赖于出汗来调节温度。当汗水从皮肤蒸发时，它会带走热量，帮助身体保持凉爽。当湿度很高时，蒸发就不起作用了，身体更难释放热量并保持凉爽。

paragraphs.en: Humid conditions can boost the risk of heat-related illnesses such as heatstroke, worsen existing heart and lung conditions and put more strain on the bodies of people with chronic diseases.
paragraphs.zh: 潮湿的环境会增加中暑等与热有关的疾病的风险，使现有的心脏和肺部状况恶化，并给慢性病患者的身体带来更多的压力。

paragraphs.en: High humidity can also contribute to poor sleep, reducing the body’s ability to recover during prolonged hot periods.
paragraphs.zh: 高湿度也会导致睡眠不佳，降低身体在长时间炎热期间的恢复能力。

paragraphs.en: Hot and wet conditions also provide optimal conditions for mosquitoes, ticks and parasites, which are vectors for the spread of key tropical diseases. Mould, bacteria and viruses are more likely to grow in high humidity, increasing the risk of lung and skin disease.
paragraphs.zh: 炎热和潮湿的条件也为蚊子、蜱虫和寄生虫提供了最佳条件，这些都是主要热带疾病传播的媒介。霉菌、细菌和病毒更容易在高湿度下生长，增加了肺部和皮肤病的风险。

paragraphs.en: What we found in the Northern Territory
paragraphs.zh: 我们在北领地发现的

paragraphs.en: The top third of the Northern Territory has a monsoonal coastal climate prone to humidity, while the two thirds inland is arid. This means we can analyse and compare humid and dry heatwaves across these environments.
paragraphs.zh: 北领地的上三分之一属于季风性沿海气候，容易潮湿，而内陆的三分之二则是干旱的。这意味着我们可以分析和比较这些环境中的潮湿和干燥热浪。

paragraphs.en: Our study analysed more than two decades of emergency department data across the NT to see if dry heat or humid heat affected the numbers of people needing emergency care. We used a temperature-based index for dry heat and a combined temperature and relative humidity index to determine humid heat.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究分析了超过20年的急诊科数据在整个NT，看看是否干热或湿热影响需要紧急护理的人数。我们使用了基于温度的干热指数和温度和相对湿度的综合指数来确定湿热。

paragraphs.en: The results were clear. While more people sought emergency treatment during both dry and humid heatwaves, humid heatwaves were worse. Severe and extreme dry heatwaves led to 4.4% more hospital visits, while similar humid heatwaves saw 6.1% more people attending emergency departments.
paragraphs.zh: 结果很明显。尽管在干热和湿热天气下寻求紧急治疗的人更多，但湿热天气更糟糕。严重和极端干热天气导致医院就诊人数增加4.4%，而类似的湿热天气导致急诊室就诊人数增加6.1%。

paragraphs.en: When arid areas of the Territory were hit by humid heatwaves, the effect was even clearer – emergency visits rose 8.7%.
paragraphs.zh: 当该领土的干旱地区遭受潮湿热浪袭击时，影响更加明显-紧急访问增加了8.7%。

paragraphs.en: Where are the warnings?
paragraphs.zh: 警告在哪里？

paragraphs.en: In many parts of northern Australia, heatwaves are projected to become more frequent and intense due to global warming.
paragraphs.zh: 在澳大利亚北方的许多地区，由于全球变暖，热浪预计将变得更加频繁和强烈。

paragraphs.en: Every summer, Australia’s Bureau of Meteorology issues heatwave warnings to give people advance notice of three or more days of unusual heat over day and night. Warnings can be issued for mild, severe and extreme heatwaves.
paragraphs.zh: 每年夏天，澳大利亚气象局都会发布热浪警报，提前通知人们三天或三天以上的白天和黑夜的异常高温。热浪警报可以针对轻度、重度和极端热浪发布。

paragraphs.en: These warnings are vital. They let people prepare for heat and change plans, while health services can boost staffing numbers.
paragraphs.zh: 这些警告是至关重要的。它们让人们为高温做好准备并改变计划，而卫生服务部门可以增加员工人数。

paragraphs.en: The problem is, these warnings are largely based on temperature. Most people can tolerate a 35°C day with low humidity. But a 35°C day with high humidity is much harder for us to cope with.
paragraphs.zh: 问题是，这些警告很大程度上是基于温度。大多数人可以忍受35°C的低湿度天气。但35°C的高湿度天气对我们来说要难得多。

paragraphs.en: This means the current system may not be warning Australians about a real risk to their health – especially those in tropical and coastal regions.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着目前的系统可能没有警告澳大利亚人对他们的健康有真实的风险--特别是那些在热带和沿海地区的人。

paragraphs.en: Preparing health services for humid heat
paragraphs.zh: 为湿热做好卫生服务准备

paragraphs.en: Health services in the NT are often ageing and under strain. Last wet season did significant damage.
paragraphs.zh: 北部地区的卫生服务经常老化和紧张，上一个雨季造成了严重的破坏。

paragraphs.en: Dry and wet heatwaves will put more pressure on health systems already struggling during extreme weather. Even a modest increase in patients will add more pressure on staffing, bed capacity and resources.
paragraphs.zh: 干湿热浪将给已经在极端天气中苦苦挣扎的卫生系统带来更大压力。即使是病人数量的小幅增加，也会给人员配备、床位容量和资源带来更大压力。

paragraphs.en: We’ve long known heat affects some people much more than others. Children, older adults, people with chronic diseases and those in disadvantaged communities are hit harder. In the Territory, low-quality housing, poor access to healthcare and outdoor work and recreation also boost risks from heat.
paragraphs.zh: 我们早就知道高温对某些人的影响要比其他人大得多。儿童、老年人、慢性病患者和弱势社区的人受到的影响更大。在该地区，低质量的住房、难以获得医疗保健以及户外工作和娱乐也增加了高温的风险。

paragraphs.en: Time to redefine heatwaves
paragraphs.zh: 是时候重新定义热浪了

paragraphs.en: It’s no longer enough to define a heatwave using temperature alone. Across northern Australia, humidity directly affects how people experience a heatwave.
paragraphs.zh: 仅仅用温度来定义热浪已经不够了。在澳大利亚北方，湿度直接影响人们对热浪的感受。

paragraphs.en: Climatologists are already exploring ways to include humidity in measures of dangerous heat.
paragraphs.zh: 气候学家已经在探索将湿度纳入危险热量测量的方法。

paragraphs.en: To take the threat of humid heat seriously, we need to redefine heatwaves to include humidity and temperature. This will strengthen our early warning systems.
paragraphs.zh: 为了认真对待湿热的威胁，我们需要重新定义热浪，将湿度和温度包括在内。这将加强我们的早期预警系统。

paragraphs.en: On a practical level, we need to prepare our health systems for more demand during severe humid heat, particularly in remote and tropical regions.
paragraphs.zh: 在实际层面上，我们需要使我们的卫生系统做好准备，以应对极端湿热时期的更多需求，特别是在偏远和热带地区。

paragraphs.en: As the Top End prepares for another wet season, authorities will focus on the threats of cyclones, flooding and other visible weather threats. It’s time to look at a less visible danger – the combination of heat and humidity.
paragraphs.zh: 随着高端为另一个雨季做准备，当局将重点关注飓风、洪水和其他可见天气威胁的威胁。现在是时候关注一个不太明显的危险了--高温和潮湿的结合。
